questions.stem:
A rugby club coach uses club records to take a random sample of 15 players from 1990 and an independent random sample of 15 players from 2010. The body weight of each player was recorded to the nearest kg and the results from 2010 are summarised in the table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Body weight (kg)} & 75\text{–}79 & 80\text{–}84 & 85\text{–}89 & 90\text{–}94 & 95\text{–}99 & 100\text{–}104 & 105\text{–}109\\ \hline \text{Number of Players (2010)} & 1 & 2 & 2 & 4 & 3 & 2 & 1\\ \hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the estimated values in kg of the summary statistics $a$, $b$ and $c$ in the table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline & \text{Estimate in 1990} & \text{Estimate in 2010}\\ \hline \text{Mean} & 83.0 & a\\ \hline \text{Median} & 82.0 & b\\ \hline \text{Variance} & 44.0 & c\\ \hline\end{array}$

Give your answers to 3 significant figures.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $a = \dfrac{77\times 1+82\times 2+...}{15} = \dfrac{1385}{15} = \dfrac{277}{3} = 92.\dot{3}$ awrt 92.3 M1 A1
$b = \left[89.5+\right]\dfrac{7.5-5}{9-5}(94.5-89.5) = 92.625$ awrt 92.6 M1 A1
$c = \dfrac{1\times 77^2+2\times 82^2.....}{15}-92.\dot{3}^2 = 64.88...$ awrt 64.9 M1 A1

Notes: NB mid points are: 77, 82, 87, 92, 97, 102, 107.
1st M1 for attempt to use correct midpoints in an expression for mean. Accept $\dfrac{\sum fx}{15}$ with at least 3 correct fx products seen and intention to add, or $1300<\sum fx<1400$.
1st A1 for awrt 92.3 (don't insist on 3 sf).
2nd M1 for $\dfrac{7.5-5}{9-5}(94.5-89.5)$ or $\dfrac{8-5}{9-5}(94.5-89.5)$. May see them come down from the top of the interval, look out for $\left[94.5-\right]\dfrac{9-7.5}{9-5}(94.5-89.5)$ or $\left[94.5-\right]\dfrac{9-8}{9-5}(94.5-89.5)$. Correct end point and [..] not needed for M1 i.e. M1 is for correct fraction x correct class width.
2nd A1 for awrt 92.6. For n+1 case (gives 93.25 so allow awrt 93.3) don't insist on 3sf. The correct answer must not follow from an incorrect expression.
3rd M1 for a fully correct expression ft their a e.g. $\dfrac{128855}{15}-a^2$ or $\dfrac{25771}{3}-a^2$.
3rd A1 for awrt 64.9 (Accept $s^2=69.5238...$ or awrt 69.5). Don't insist on 3sf.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Correct answer only in part (a) scores full marks and answers must be decimals not fractions

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The rugby coach claims that players' body weight increased between 1990 and 2010.
(b) Using the table in part (a), comment on the rugby coach's claim.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Median in 2010 (92.6 kg) > Median in 1990 (82.0 kg)
Mean in 2010 (92.3 kg) > Mean in 1990 (83.0 kg) either B1
Rugby coach's claim supported. dep dB1

Notes: 1st B1 for a suitable reason i.e. identifying an increase in mean or median. Ignore any comment about variance.
2nd dB1 dependent on a suitable reason for stating that the coach's claim is supported. Allow these marks provided both their a > 83.0 and their b > 82.0. If it is NOT the case that both a > 83.0 and b > 82.0 then allow a ft provided M1 scored for both a and b in part (a).

questions.stem:
A group of 100 students are asked if they like folk music, rock music or soul music.
All students who like folk music also like rock music
No students like both rock music and soul music
75 students do not like soul music
12 students who like rock music do not like folk music
30 students like folk music

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a Venn diagram to illustrate this information.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) [Venn diagram: three labelled loops S, F, R with F inside R; F∩R region 30, R\F region 12, S separate loop 25, outside all 33]
1st B1 for 3 labelled loops and a box. The 33 is not required for any marks in (a).
2nd B1 for $F \subset R$ or indicated by zeros.
3rd B1 for 30 and 12 correctly placed and $n(F)=30$ and $n(F'\cap R)=12$.
4th B1 for S a separate loop, or indicated by zeros, and the 25.

Note: In the diagram do not treat a blank space as zero. Allow probabilities or integers.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) State two of these types of music that are mutually exclusive.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:

Note: B1 for a correct pair. If there is more than one pair then each pair must be correct. Do not allow P(F) etc or e.g. P($R\cap S$) = 0

parts.label: e

questions.stem: A manufacturer has a machine that fills bags with flour such that the weight of flour in a bag is normally distributed. A label states that each bag should contain 1 kg of flour.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) The machine is set so that the weight of flour in a bag has mean 1.04 kg and standard deviation 0.17 kg. Find the proportion of bags that weigh less than the stated weight of 1 kg.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $[X\sim\mathrm{N}(1.04, 0.17^2)]$
$\mathrm{P}(X<1)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z<\dfrac{1-1.04}{0.17}\right)$ M1
$=\mathrm{P}(Z<-0.23529...)$
$=1-0.5948=0.4052$ (Accept 0.405-0.407) M1A1

Notes: 1st M1 for attempting to standardise with 1, 1.04 and 0.17. Allow $\pm$.
2nd M1 for attempting $1-p$ where ($0.5<p<0.6$).
A1 for answers in the range 0.405~0.407 (Calc gives 0.4069902…)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The manufacturer wants to reduce the number of bags which contain less than the stated weight of 1 kg. At first she decides to adjust the mean but not the standard deviation so that only 5% of the bags filled are below the stated weight of 1 kg.
(b) Find the adjusted mean.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $[Y\sim\mathrm{N}(\mu, 0.17^2)]$
$\mathrm{P}(Y<1)=0.05$
$\dfrac{1-\mu}{0.17}=-1.6449$ M1 B1
$\mu=1+1.6449\times 0.17=1.2796...$ awrt 1.28 A1

Notes: M1 for an attempt to standardise (allow $\pm$) with 1, 0.17 and $\mu$ and set = $\pm$ any z value ($|z|>1$).
B1 for $z=\pm 1.6449$ (or better. Calc gives 1.6448536..) used as a z value. Do not allow $1-1.6449$ [May be implied by answer that rounds to 1.2796]
A1 for awrt 1.28 (can be scored for using a z value of 1.64 or 1.65). Must follow from correct working but a range of possible z values are OK.
If answer is awrt 1.28 score M1B0A1 (unless of course z = 1.6449 seen) but awrt 1.2796 scores 3/3.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Allow any alternative letters to $\mu$ and $\sigma$ in parts (b) and (c)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The manufacturer finds that a lot of the bags are overflowing with flour when the mean is adjusted, so decides to adjust the standard deviation instead to make the machine more accurate. The machine is set back to a mean of 1.04 kg. The manufacturer wants 1% of bags to be under 1 kg.
(c) Find the adjusted standard deviation. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $[S\sim\mathrm{N}(1.04, \sigma^2)]$
$\mathrm{P}(S<1)=0.01$
$\dfrac{1-1.04}{\sigma}=-2.3263$ M1B1
$\sigma=\dfrac{0.04}{2.3263}=0.0171946...$ awrt 0.0172 A1

Notes: M1 for an attempt to standardise with 1, 1.04 and $\sigma$ and set = $\pm$ any z value ($|z|>2$).
B1 for $z=\pm 2.3263$ (or better) (Calc gives 2.3263478…) used as a z value. If B0 scored in (b) for using a value in [1.64, 1.65] but not 1.6449 or better, allow awrt 2.32 or 2.33 here.
A1 for awrt 0.0172. Must follow from correct working but a range of possible z values are OK.
If answer is awrt 0.0172 score M1B0A1 (unless of course z = 2.3263 or better is seen). If B1 scored in (b) and z = 2.3263 or better is not seen here then require an answer in the range 0.17194 < $\sigma$ < 0.17195 to award 3/3.

questions.stem:
In a large college, $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of the students are male, $\dfrac{3}{10}$ of the students are left handed and $\dfrac{1}{5}$ of the male students are left handed.
A student is chosen at random.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Given that the student is left handed, find the probability that the student is male.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $[\mathrm{P}(M|L)]=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(M\cap L)}{\mathrm{P}(L)}=\dfrac{\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{1}{5}}{\frac{3}{10}}$ M1
$=0.40$ (o.e) A1

Note: M1 for a fully correct ratio e.g. $\dfrac{0.12}{0.30}$ or a correct ratio expression and one correct prob. If numerator > denominator then M0.
A1 for 0.40 or any exact equivalent.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Given that the student is female, find the probability that she is left handed.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $x=[\mathrm{P}(L|F)]=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(L\cap F)}{\mathrm{P}(F)}=\dfrac{\frac{3}{10}-\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{1}{5}}{1-\frac{3}{5}}$ or $\dfrac{3}{5}\times\dfrac{1}{5}+\left(1-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\times x=\dfrac{3}{10}$ M1
$x=\dfrac{0.3-0.12}{0.40}$ or $0.4x=0.3-0.12$ M1
$x=0.45$ (o.e.) A1

Notes: 1st M1 for an equation for x with at least 2 of: $\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\times\dfrac{1}{5}\right)$ or $\dfrac{3}{10}$ or $\left(1-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)$ correct BUT $\dfrac{\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{3}{10}}{\frac{2}{5}}$ is M0 or allow M1 for $\mathrm{P}(L\cap F)=0.18$.
2nd M1 for a fully correct expression for x = … or 0.4x = …
A1 for 0.45 or any exact equivalent.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the probability that the randomly chosen student is male and right handed.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $[\mathrm{P}(M\cap R)]=0.6-\mathrm{P}(M\cap L)$ or $0.6\times(1-0.2)$ M1
$=0.48$ (o.e.) A1

Note: M1 for a correct expression with 0.6 follow through their $\mathrm{P}(M\cap L)=0.12$.
A1 for 0.48 or any exact equivalent.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Two students are chosen at random.
(d) Find the probability that one student is left handed and one is right handed.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $\mathrm{P}(\text{one is left handed and the other right handed}) = 2\times\dfrac{3}{10}\times\dfrac{7}{10} = \dfrac{21}{50}$ or 0.42 M1, A1

Note: M1 for a fully correct expression including the 2. Allow $1-0.3$ instead of $0.7$.
A1 for 0.42 or any exact equivalent.

NB You may see Venn or tree diagram drawn but marks are given when values are used in correct expressions as above.

questions.stem:
A manager records the number of hours of overtime claimed by 40 staff in a month.
The histogram in Figure 1 represents the results.
[Histogram: Frequency density on y-axis; Hours of overtime on x-axis with bars over intervals 0–2, 2–5, 5–10, 10–20, 20–30]

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Calculate the number of staff who have claimed less than 10 hours of overtime in the month.
(4)

(a) Total area of bars = 400 small squares B1
